Change has been successfully merged

Since a flexible array must appear only at the end of a structure and there can be at most one per struct, the cleanest approach here would be to use a count + pointer design and allocate the variable-sized data using separate malloc calls. This is just a suggestion—there may be other valid ways to implement it, but this seems the most appropriate given the constraints.

Related discussion here:

https://discord.com/channels/775381525260664832/1464377017834147872/1471660017374593200
Please review the new version with the iterator approach
Done
I didn't find any standard way in libpldm how to deal with such dynamic information inside the PDR structure. If there is a better way, please advice how to do it properly libpldm-style.
Done

Just noting the request to split this change up a bit here:

https://discord.com/channels/775381525260664832/1464377017834147872/1473538066366074901

For the complete implementation we need 4 iterators.

I've left this patchset with just decode functions, and pushed the patchset for the 1 of the 4 required iterators to the `87536: dsp: platform: Add Redfish actions iterator API` | https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/87536

Once we solve all the issues I'll push the other 3 ones.

This is the part that is labeled `Action Information` area in the specification.

It contains
```
  ActionCount
  ActionNameLengthBytes [0]
  ActionName [0]
  ActionPathLengthBytes [0]
  ...
  ActionNameLengthBytes [N]
  ActionName [N]
  ActionPathLengthBytes [N]
```
It is also returned in the `pldm_platform_redfish_action_pdr.action_info`.

I think I find it lacking that in case of the `foreach` API that we implement there is no easy way to get `ActionCount` without full iterating.

What is preffered way to add this?
1) add `uint8_t action_count` to the pdr structure
2) add `uint8_t action_count` to the action_info structure
3) create another API to get it from the action_info structure

The easiest way is 1/2, in case we do that, do we need to move area.ptr after the `ActionCount` field, or can we leave things as they are?
Count field are now in the PDR structure
Why are we doing both in the one change? Is there a concern with splitting this into separate changes? Because that would be my preference in terms of making this straight-forward to review.
I've split the patches for the Redfish Resource/Action PDRs
Can you please include the section number as well?
Done
I've only reviewed the Redfish Resource PDR portion for now. Please see the comment about splitting the change to deal with the Redfish Action PDR.
In the spirit of "keep things that go together together", my current preference is we define these length macros immediately below the relevant struct.
Done
Perhaps `additional_resources` rather than `additional_resource_info`
Let's add a struct member to capture the additional resource count. See comment on the implementation.

Can you please clarify, should the `struct variable_field additional_resource_info` area still include the `additional resource count` field or should we move `additional_resource_info.ptr` in this case?

1) If we don't move it, this creates a little duplication between the fields, is this ok?

2) If we move it, I'm not sure how to extract the ptr with the current msgbuf API

I guess this question would be resolved based on the thread https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/87283/comment/b25a0199_4fc08383/

But for a little bit of explanation, this was done based on these things:
1) `struct variable_field additional_resource_info;` currently includes both count field and all the records
2) For some reason this is not the case for Redfish Resource PDR, but in the Redfish Action PDR (Table 106) such areas representing both count field and records are grouped in the table as `Host Resource Information`/`Action Information`.

Sure. If the current msgbuf APIs don't meet our needs, we can always add to them.

What do you think of this sketch?

https://gist.github.com/amboar/23781873e3aba5c7c49cef3bf0ae4503
My preference is the naming should match the spec, even if the spec is not consistent with itself 😊

Since now this `variable_field` inside the PDR structure doesn't have the `count` field in itself, I've renamed it to the `additional_resources` as you've requested.

At the same time I've left the `additional_resource_info` name for the structure that is used in the iterators, since it has both count and records
Thanks! I think that is exactly what was needed. I've added msgbuf changes to the patchset `87913: msgbuf: Add pldm_msgbuf_field_begin/end` | https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/87913
`oem_names` to reflect `additional_resources` above.
Add a struct member to record the oem count as with the additional resource count above.
Done

nit: I suggest using a imperative mood

```suggestion
- platform: Add functions to decode Redfish Resource PDR (DSP0248 v1.3.0)
```

https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/git/git.git/tree/Documentation/SubmittingPatches

```
Describe your changes in imperative mood, e.g. "make xyzzy do frotz"
instead of "[This patch] makes xyzzy do frotz" or "[I] changed xyzzy
to do frotz", as if you are giving orders to the codebase to change
its behavior.
```

Honestly `Added` looks strange to me too, but this style is used all over the CHANGELOG.md. Maybe the rule above is not applicable in this case, because `CHANGELOG != commit`. Let's wait for the maintainers response
